paper.title: From Simulated Citizens to Simulated Deliberation: Challenges in Representation and Interaction

findings.title: Persona answers miss the survey map
findings.body: On 640 census-balanced Korean personas, GPT-4.1-mini's mean absolute gap from human group shares is 29 points. Every demographic group's mean gap sits between 24 and 34 points.

findings.title: Demographic direction is often reversed
findings.body: When the human survey has one group higher than another, the personas match that direction in 34 of 110 comparisons. On the two relatively split questions the match is 9 of 28.

findings.title: Answers pile up near 0% or 100%
findings.body: On five of eight questions at least one demographic group is near 0 or 100, while the matching human shares stay closer to the middle. Only climate technology (63%) and education-care (62%) stay inside the paper's 65% 'divisive' cutoff.

findings.title: Sealed monologues land in the same place
findings.body: In balanced rooms, the mean gap between full debate and sealed monologue final A counts is at most one agent out of six. Much of the observed stance movement can arise without peer exchange.

findings.title: Restating a starting side freezes updating
findings.body: When round 1 names the assigned side, movement falls to 0 to 3% in most cells. A fully argued opening is not required for that freeze. Anchoring population-informed starts also stalls updating.

findings.title: Treat argument surfacing as a separate job
findings.body: The transcripts still give reasons on both sides, and argument counts rise across rounds. That can help a reader inspect arguments. It does not show that the room represents a population, or that peer exchange caused the stance changes.

replication.note: The paper used 640 personas (4 per cell) and GPT-4.1-mini. This folder uses a jointly balanced pool (1 persona per cell). Survey and debate rows below come from a deterministic dummy client calibrated to the paper's GPT-4.1-mini overall A-shares, because a full live Qwen run was not used for this payload.

takeaways.title: Persona answers miss the survey map
takeaways.body: Across demographic groups, the mean absolute gap between a dummy client calibrated to the paper's overall GPT-4.1-mini A-shares and the human surveys is 28.7 points. The paper reported 29 points with GPT-4.1-mini on 640 personas.

takeaways.title: Demographic direction is often reversed
takeaways.body: When the human survey has one group higher than another, the personas match that direction in 50 of 105 comparisons. The paper matched 34 of 110.

takeaways.title: Answers pile up near 0% or 100%
takeaways.body: 22 demographic cells land within 2 points of 0 or 100, while the matching human shares stay closer to the middle.

takeaways.title: Sealed monologues land in the same place
takeaways.body: Dummy rooms are a protocol walkthrough with hash-based replies, not a language-model interaction test. In the paper, sealed monologue rooms ended within one agent of full debate.

takeaways.title: Restating a starting side freezes updating
takeaways.body: Dummy movement does not drop when round 1 restates the assigned side. In the paper, restating the side cut later movement to 0 to 3%.

takeaways.title: Treat argument surfacing as a separate job
takeaways.body: The transcripts still give reasons on both sides. That can help a reader inspect arguments. It does not show that the room represents a population, or that peer exchange caused the stance changes.
